title: Neo4j Small Examples
description: Use these small Neo4j examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Create a node with a label
examples.description: A node represents one thing. A label says what kind of thing it is, and properties hold its named facts.
examples.output: A Book node is created and Moon Trip is returned.

examples.title: Find a node by a property
examples.description: MATCH finds graph patterns. A property condition can choose the node with a known id.
examples.output: The previously created book returns its title and 60 pages.

examples.title: Add a uniqueness rule
examples.description: A uniqueness constraint prevents two nodes with a label from sharing the same chosen property value.
examples.code: CREATE CONSTRAINT cma_book_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (b:Book) REQUIRE b.id IS UNIQUE;
examples.output: Neo4j creates the constraint if the existing Book ids satisfy it.

examples.title: Match or create with MERGE
examples.description: MERGE finds a pattern or creates it if missing.
examples.code: MERGE (b:Book {id:'cma-b2'}) SET b.title='Garden Days',b.pages=40 RETURN b.title;
examples.output: The book with id cma-b2 is created or updated with the title Garden Days.

examples.title: Connect a reader to a book
examples.description: A relationship gives two nodes a named connection and direction.
examples.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r1'}) SET r.name='Mia'
WITH r MATCH (b:Book {id:'cma-b1'}) MERGE (r)-[:READ]->(b) RETURN r.name,b.title;
examples.output: Mia is connected to Moon Trip by an outgoing READ relationship.

examples.title: Follow a relationship
examples.description: A pattern can follow a known relationship to related nodes.
examples.output: The result lists the books connected to Mia through READ.

examples.title: Filter nodes with WHERE
examples.description: WHERE adds a condition to a matched pattern.
examples.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH "cma-" AND b.pages>=50 RETURN b.title,b.pages;
examples.output: The sample 60-page Moon Trip matches, while the 40-page Garden Days does not.

examples.title: Sort and limit graph results
examples.description: ORDER BY sorts returned rows from a graph query.
examples.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH 'cma-' RETURN b.title,b.pages ORDER BY b.pages,b.title LIMIT 1;
examples.output: With the two sample books, Garden Days is the shortest result.

examples.title: Count connected books
examples.description: An aggregate can summarise matched relationships.
examples.output: Mia has one matched book in the seeded graph.

examples.title: Keep a reader with no match
examples.description: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps the earlier row even when the optional connection is missing.
examples.code:
MERGE (r:Reader {id:'cma-r2'}) SET r.name='Sam'
WITH r OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:READ]->(b:Book) RETURN r.name,b.title;
examples.output: Sam is returned with a null book title if no READ relationship exists.

examples.title: Change a relationship fact
examples.description: Relationships can hold properties too. A property can describe the connection itself, such as when a reader finished a book.
examples.output: The READ relationship receives the finish date.

examples.title: Remove one practice node carefully
examples.description: A connected node cannot be deleted normally while its relationships remain.
examples.output: Only the sample reader cma-r2 and its own connections are removed.
